description.narrative: The Additional Financing (AF) under the RMI Urban Resilience Project (RMIURP) is designed to scale up and consolidate a proven, multi-sectoral approach to strengthening urban resilience in the Republic of the Marshall Islands by deepening ongoing reforms and financing priority investments in high-risk urban areas, particularly Majuro. The AF builds on existing project components by expanding risk-informed urban planning and building code implementation, advancing coastal protection and resilient public space investments, upgrading critical public and emergency facilities, and strengthening disaster preparedness and response systems, while ensuring continued support for project management and institutional capacity. The design emphasizes integration of long-term policy and institutional reforms with targeted, climate-resilient infrastructure and community-focused interventions, responding to rising climate and disaster risks, rapid urbanization, and demonstrated financing gaps needed to meet the project's development objectives and results indicators.
To strengthen the resilience of select urban areas in the Republic of the Marshall Islands to the impacts of natural hazards and climate change

condition.narrative: Schedule 2, Section I.A.1: The Recipient shall establish no later than three (3) months after the Effective Date, and thereaftermaintain, throughout Project implementation period, a Steering Committee, with a mandate and composition acceptable to theAssociation.

Schedule 2, Section I.A.2: The Recipient shall establish no later than four (4) months after the Effective Date, and thereaftermaintain, throughout the Project implementation period, the Technical Working Group, with a mandate, composition and resourcessatisfactory to the Association.

Schedule 2, Section I.A.3: The Recipient shall establish no later than three (3) months after the Effective Date, and thereaftermaintain, throughout the Project implementation period, a Project Implementation Unit (PIU), within the MWIU, with a mandate,composition and resources satisfactory to the Association.

Schedule 2, Section I.A.4: The Recipient shall, no later than three (3) months after the Effective Date, recruit and thereaftermaintain, an engineer and a project manager, each with terms of reference, qualifications, and experience satisfactory to theAssociation.

Schedule 2, Section I.B.1: The Recipient shall, by not later than one (1) month after the Effective Date (or such other date whichthe Association has confirmed in writing to the Recipient is reasonable and acceptable under the circumstances, as determined bytheAssociation in its sole discretion) prepare and furnish to the Association for its review and no-objection a Project OperationsManual.

Schedule 2, Section I.C.1: The Recipient shall prepare and furnish to the Association's review and no-objection, by not later than:(a) two (2) months after the Effective Date (or such later date which, after consideration of the reasons for the delay, theAssociation has confirmed in writing is acceptable to the Association in its sole discretion); and (b) June 15 of each year forevery subsequent year during the implementation of the Project (or such later date which, after consideration of the reasons forthe delay, the Association has confirmed in writing is acceptable to the Association in its sole discretion); an Annual Work Planand Budget.
Schedule 2, Section II.1:The Recipient shall furnish to the Association each Project Report not later than forty-five (45) daysafter the end of each semester, covering the semester.

Schedule 2, Section II.2: The Recipient shall carry out, jointly with the Association, not later than three (3) years after theEffective Date, or such other period as may be agreed with the Association, a mid-term review of the Project (“Mid-Term Review”) toassess the status of Project implementation, as measured against the indicators acceptable to the Association, and compliance withthe legal covenants included or referred to in this Agreement.

title.narrative: Number of stakeholders trained on climate resilient and inclusive urban planning through participatory planning initiatives and workshops

comment.narrative: Progress under this indicator shows a total of 17 training/knowledge sharing activities conducted with 156 stakeholders on climate resilient and inclusive urban planning. This figure excludes new stakeholders from the College of the Marshall Is., who are scheduled to participate in a knowledge-sharing session on urban and marine studies in early October. This figure only counts each training participant once, i.e., does not “double count” participants if they participated in more than one training.

title.narrative: People provided with improved urban living conditions

comment.narrative: Progress under this indicator reflects the cleaning, assessment, and repair of urban drainage from Rita to Bridge, covering a total cleaned length of 14,943 meters. The section from EZ Price to Home Garden were excluded due to high-voltage MEC lines running through the drainage. Another section from MoNRC to the MEC tank farm was also excluded due to oil spillage concerns. In total, the project has cleaned the drains that directly abut 371 houses. The average family size in the Marshall Islands is 5.8. The project has therefore improved the living conditions of approximately 2,152 people.

title.narrative: Issues and complaints raised in the project's feedback and grievance redress mechanism addressed within 21 calendar days

comment.narrative: Progress under this indicator shows that 2 grievances were formally recorded in the project's Feedback and Grievances Redress Mechanism (FGRM) registry. All complaints were addressed and resolved within five (5) working days, and corresponding work commenced. This demonstrates timely responsiveness to stakeholder concerns within the project's established 21-calendar-day target.

title.narrative: Women beneficiaries in project areas who report that the project activities regarding reduced climate and disaster risks in coastal urban settlements reflect their needs

comment.narrative: This indicator aims to demonstrate that project activities under Components 1, 2 and 3 have been planned and implemented through a beneficiaries-focused participatory approach and that the increased representation of women in decision making processes results in activities that more closely respond to women's needs. A beneficiary survey was conducted of the drainage cleaning activity and a 100% satisfaction rate was recorded for female respondents. This indicator is in compliance with the World Bank's corporate commitment on citizen engagement.
